Bible study for beginners: your first session

Choose a short, complete passage for your first session. Read it, ask questions, and check your answers against the text itself.

Read Luke 10 at eBible.org, World English Bible

Four steps for a first Bible study

  • Read the whole passage and look at what comes before and after it.
  • Notice the people, actions and repeated words.
  • Separate what the passage states from your own assumptions.
  • Summarise the main idea and write one question or practical response.

A worked example: the Good Samaritan

Open Luke 10:25-37. Before the parable, a conversation begins with a question about eternal life and then about who counts as a neighbour. Read that conversation as well as the story.

Who notices the injured man? Who passes by? What does the Samaritan do? Look for answers in verses 30-35, then compare the original question in verse 29 with Jesus’ question in verse 36.

  • Observation: the Samaritan approaches, cares for the man and pays for further help.
  • A question about meaning: why does the conversation end by asking who became a neighbour?
  • A personal response: whom could I help through a concrete action? Keep your response distinct from a quotation of Scripture.

Continue with context

In your next session, return to the surrounding passages in Luke. If a word, historical detail or idea is unclear, record the question and consult a reliable commentary or discuss it with a mentor. Christian traditions may interpret particular passages differently.

This is a standalone introductory session on the website. It is not the full Chrust course and does not mark an app lesson as completed.
